pr_title: Configuration variables for GitHub Actions impl: set
pr_body: Set(create/update) variables operation added through this PR. Modes supported: `body` and `prompt`. Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/6836
pr_comments: Hi! Thanks for the pull request. Please ensure that this change is linked to an issue by mentioning an issue number in the description of the pull request. If this pull request would close the issue, please put the word 'Fixes' before the issue number somewhere in the pull request body. If this is a tiny change like fixing a typo, feel free to ignore this message.

@samcoe Regarding sharing functionalities between secrets and variables, in pse review, it was outlined for variables functionality to be hard separated from secrets in order to avoid security issues. Even though similar in operations, secrets are encrypted and are considered entirely different entities from variables. Also, from the API front, there are differences, eg. secrets are required to be encrypted by user using [scoped](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/secrets?apiVersion=2022-11-28#create-or-update-an-organization-secret) public key, whereas no such requirement exists in variables.
I have converted this PR to create only. list and other commands to follow in separate PRs.

@samcoe  Follow PRs for each operation:
list: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/6995
delete: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/6929
update: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/6997

@atirikt Thanks for the hard work on making the requested changes! I pushed a commit to help simplify the implementation of this command considerably. The things I changed:
1. No longer require retrieving variables to determine if we should do a create or update. Now the command will try to create the variable and if that fails with a 409 we will do an update.
2. Changed from supporting CSV files to ENV files, which is what we support in the `secret` command. We don't have any other commands that support CSV so I thought it was more appropriate to keep with standards we already have in place.
3. Removed additional prompts for visibility and confirmation.
4. Shared some common API functionality, `MapReposToIDs`, between `variable` and `secret` commands.
5. Cleaned up unused code and simplified the tests a bit.
Accidentally pushed the closed button, sorry about that.

issue_context.title: Add support for setting configuration variables (actions)
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

Starting from today, GitHub supports configuration variables: https://github.blog/changelog/2023-01-10-github-actions-support-for-configuration-variables-in-workflows/
It's something that is currently missing in GitHub cli.

### Proposed solution

It would be nice to have an option to set configuration variables in a similar way as `gh secret`. I'm pretty sure many users will appreciate that.

### Additional context

None.
comments:
Good idea.

The UX for this should map to `gh secret`.

See: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/variables?apiVersion=2022-11-28

An important consideration is a friendly and clear error message if the API endpoint doesn't exist, which will be true of recent GitHub Enterprise versions.

review_comments:
Should this be added to the group of commands for actions?

```
gh actions
```

The command is following the `secrets` model of implementation, variables, in the future, may support more integrations(like secrets does for `dependabot` and `codespaces` today along with actions), therefore did not want to tie it to actions integration only.

Thank you for that additional insight! 🙇 

I originally presumed that a command might be able to live in multiple groups, however I'm not 💯 sure there as looking at [`workflow` base command](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/88711201ae886b45ebab320a6cb5ff72f681854a/pkg/cmd/workflow/workflow.go#L13-L19) shows a singular group.

https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/88711201ae886b45ebab320a6cb5ff72f681854a/pkg/cmd/workflow/workflow.go#L13-L19

All that to say, I've got nothing additional to share as a CLI groupie ❤️  Feel free to resolve conversation
